**Status:** ❓ Needs testing. All profiles are hardware UNVERIFIED; qualification is for existing owners after an external beta or release.

## Features

| Feature | Supported |
|---------|-----------|
| Motor control | Model-selected back, feet, waist, neck, independent lifts or storage lift |
| Position feedback | No motor angle or percentage parser |
| Memory | Two recall/save slots where the selected screen provides them |
| Presets | ZZ (anti-snore-labelled icon), TV and zero gravity on selected models |
| Massage | Conventional vibration, AS relative sonic controls, I/HI sonic zones/modes/level |
| Lighting | On/off on P1, toggle on P2, RGB and brightness on RGB layouts |
| Split sides | Five catalog keys, one receiver; P1 foot is shared |
| Bed sensors | Signed sleep fields and sleep MAC, no invented firmware units |

## Choosing a profile

Choose **CheersSleep (com.cheers.sleep)**, then the exact model and numeric key. P1/P2 comes from that model's selected screen. The manufacturer notification branch is independent of the wire format. No advertised-name rule or PIN is used.

| P2 | Repeat100ms, bounded/renewable hold | Immediate unscoped zero-key | Command0/100/200ms; release300/400/500/500ms; interrupted counter retained | Stateful simple pages B0; navigation parent resume/destination D0 side0 |

### Aliases

There are no alternate integration bed-type aliases. Same-page catalog keys are retained individually.

## Wire codec

### Transports

<!-- generated:cheerssleep-transports -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_codec_docs.py from the codec and profile data. Edit those, not this block. -->

|---|---|---|
| Write | `6e403587-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e` | `6e403588-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e` |
| Notify | `6e403587-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e` | `6e403589-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e` |
<!-- /generated -->

### Framing and checksum

P1 is eight bytes: low-byte serial, PID, little-endian 16-bit command and little-endian 32-bit parameter. The command counter starts at one; ordinary sends preincrement, held sends increment only when the cached command changes, and sleep MAC queries postincrement. Settings use an independent postincrementing counter.

P2 normal frames contain an EE prefix, type1, literal length5, a big-endian 32-bit key, side and C0 terminator. Setting frames use type2 with opcode and three byte fields. Queries use B0 or D0 and literal length1. Side1 maps to AA, side2 to BB, other values retain their low byte. Neither format has a checksum, encryption or authenticated gate.

### Write mode

The app leaves Android's characteristic write mode unchanged. The integration uses acknowledged writes and requires the write property on the exact service/characteristic pair. Bleak owns the notification CCCD. The legacy Android local registration on WRITE does not establish a second CCCD subscription.

### Command encoders

#### Motor control

P1 rows show serial2 for comparison. The controller advances its actual counters. P2 held releases are unscoped even when the held command targets a side.

P1 split memory recalls use left6530/6531 and right6538/6539, saves left6540/6541 and right6548/6549. Split ZZ/TV/ZG use left6511–6513 and right6521–6523. Flat remains global. P2 memory saves use selectors5/6 and a setting-AA release, rather than the memory recall key.

P1 conventional massage retains local head/foot levels and wave mode. Steady levels wrap through off; wave levels wrap3 to1. Wave mode1 initializes both levels to1; off resets both. The right head wave intensity2 command is the shipped irregular `0x2401`, preserved without correction. P2 conventional buttons cycle hardware state; B0 replies provide levels/mode.

Shared RGB, brightness and sonic level settings always use side0, including split models. Position-page sonic zones and mode buttons retain their selected side. Color uses setting5, brightness setting10 and sonic setting11, followed by setting-AA release. AS sonic relative controls use channel2 decrease/increase and a normal unscoped held release; its toggle uses parameter3. I/HI absolute sonic level uses channel3.

### Responses

P1 MAC consumes PID89 bytes2–7. Sleep PID87/88 chooses left/right; flag byte2 provides snore, presence and asleep state. Heart/breath and remaining sleep fields retain signed Java byte values. Absence sets heart and breath to zero. Short unsafe app inputs are rejected safely.

B0 requires ten bytes. Light byte9 updates before side/mode filtering; massage mode is byte6 minus1, accepted only0–2, with signed head/foot levels7/8. NewNine filters only massage by selected side. The simple light-only pages do not gain massage from unused constants.

D0 requires seventeen bytes for all consumed fields. RGB4–6 is unsigned; brightness7 is signed. AS position light is byte8, I/HI light is byte16. The color-page consumer always uses byte16; separate position/color state sensors preserve both projections. RGB light entities use the color-page state. Mode uses byte12, or its low/high side nibble for Position500i. The shared control mode is bit0 of byte8. On I/HI models, physical sonic level11 is signed and clamped0–100. AS models expose their position/color light consumers and do not acquire I/HI mode/level observations. No audio fields, positions or new capabilities are inferred. Disconnect clears live observations; stale callbacks cannot update the next physical session.

### STOP and release behavior

Every held operation has an elapsed deadline and cancellation-independent cleanup bound to the original physical link. P1 sends the matching axis/group STOP after its release delay. P2 preserves the common unscoped zero-key release and the separate side-specific releases supplied by tap bursts. A fresh burst has seven writes over six callbacks; its final callback sends release twice. Interruption retains the runnable counter.

Non-split I/HI sonic mode holds schedule a D0 query200ms after release. **Position500i omits this follow-up.** Its separate side-toggle D0 query remains; NewNine queries on side change, NewEight and P1 split screens do not.

### Vectors

`tests/test_cheerssleep_vectors.py` proves the23 accepted literal vectors, complete fixed caller expansions, counters/rollover, burst persistence and parser fixtures. These are static artifact evidence, not peripheral captures.

## Profiles

### CheersSleep profile

**App:** [CheersSleep](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.cheers.sleep) v2.7.0 (40), `com.cheers.sleep`

**Status:** ❓ Hardware UNVERIFIED. Static direct BLE behavior is implemented.

#### Setup

Discovery requires the advertised service and the first manufacturer entry in sorted numeric order. ID89 adds89 to signed payload byte2; every other first ID is the direct model key. Short/unknown records are ignored. New installation, Configure and imported entries store the selected `product_type`; each side of a two-address pair owns its model setting.

For supported split keys, optional native Left/Right child devices retain side targeting. Standalone side selection initially defaults left and survives controller reconstruction. P1 shared foot and global flat remain shared. A timed foot move targeting both P1 children runs once per receiver for the requested duration; back and lumbar moves retain separate side execution. The P2 common release can affect either/both sides according to firmware; its exact physical effect remains unverified.

#### Controls

Native covers expose only the model's axes, with timed/held controls and the integration's renewable lease limits. Preset and memory entities use the actual command paths; saves require confirmation. Massage buttons, sonic level, RGB light controls, state sensors and a side select appear where the model supports them. Sleep sensors are disabled by default.

Movement, flat, memory recall and STOP clear the affected preset selection so its next press recalls the preset. A shared color-light toggle runs once per receiver per action, including when targeting both native children; position-light toggles retain per-side execution.

The `adjustable_bed.cheerssleep` action exposes the same bed controls and conditional exported P1 screens. `seven_motion` uses the split layout with its optional local `sleeper` selector (left/right), which must agree with any targeted child; `ten_*` and `newten_*` retain the ordinary P1 arrays for the selected position1–4 (all/back/feet/waist), including on split main models, and separate recall/save. These are conditional screens, not fabricated model keys. `rgb_preview`/`rgb2_preview` retain200/150ms preview delays; RGB2 uses white. Commit writes delay10–120 first and color-save500ms later. `snore_setting` and `out_of_bed_setting` write booleans. `yb_massage` accepts speed1–3 and timer parameter300 or900; the unreachable30-minute branch is unavailable.

P2 light on/off requires current feedback for the targeted light. A matching state sends nothing; the opposite state uses the native toggle and release. Unknown state or a toggle awaiting confirmation rejects desired-state requests. Use refresh to obtain feedback; commands never invent discrete P2 on/off frames.

#### State

Live state is published through declared keys. P1 massage levels are local app counters; they are not hardware feedback. P2 state comes from the active bed parsers. No firmware units are invented for raw sleep fields or the legacy delay setting.

D0 RGB feedback updates the native light immediately. Valid brightness percentages0–100 map to HA brightness0–255; out-of-domain signed bytes remain available in the raw brightness diagnostic. RGB and brightness observations are cleared when the physical session ends.

#### Limitations

Network/SSID/password/mesh administration, cloud/reports/accounts/OTA and unrelated audio/playback/bass/phone/desk/seating/accessory behavior are outside this direct BLE bed integration. Shared physical massage consumers remain supported. Dead builders, constants, the unused refresh helper and the unreachable Yb30-minute branch are not capabilities.
